title: Part 1 and Part 2 of the Constitution

blocks.text: [Article 1-4]
Article 1: Name and Territory of the Union 1(1) India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.
1(2) The States and the territories, thereof, shall be as specified in the First Schedule.
1(3) The territory of India shall comprise of- (a) The territories of the States
(b) The Union territories specified in the First Schedule; and (c) Such other territories as may be acquired in future.
India is not a Federation but a Union of States.
Term 'federation' has nowhere been mentioned in the Constitution.

Federation of State: A new entity that is formed through a treaty or an agreement between various federating units. E.g. USA — Union of States: No agreement between the Federating units (States). They do not have a right to secede from the Union. Eg. India
India is an Indestructible Union of Destructible states.
US is an indestructible union of indestructible states.
Article 2: Admission or Establishment of new States
Parliament may by law admit into the Union, or establish, new states on such terms and conditions as it thinks fit.
Article 3: Formation of new States and alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing States
Parliament may by law—
(a) form anew State by separation of territory from any State or by uniting two or more States or parts of States or by uniting any territory to a part of any State
(b) increase the area of any State
(c) diminish the area of any State
(d) alter the boundaries of any State
(e) alter the name of any State
NOTE: Bill related to subject matters given in Article 3 shall be introduced with the prior recommendation of the President, who shall refer this bill to the lepilatue of the state concerned.
5th Constitutional amendment empowered the President to set a time limit for state legislature to express its views.

State Reorganisation Act, 1956
The State Reorganisation Act of 1956 was passed based on the recommendations of the Fazl Ali Commission.
It removed the fourfold classification of states and created 14 States + 6 Union Territories, on 1st Nov, 1956
With regard to North India, it sought to divide the huge Hindi speaking belt into four states: Bihar, UP, MP, and Rajasthan.
In the east, the existing provinces could stay as they were with minor adjustments.
The commission rejected the demand for tribal states to be carved out of Bihar and Assam.
The commission did not agree with the creation of a Sikh state.

[Article 5-11]
Article 5: Citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution

A person shall be deemed to be a citizen of India on 26 January 1950, if they fulfill any of the following condition- (a) Born in India (b) Either of the parents was born in India or, (c) Has been an ordinary resident of India for at least 5 years immediately before 26 January, 1950 Single citizenship: Taken from UK (Britain)
Article 6: Persons who migrated from Pakistan to India before 19 July 1948 were granted citizenship automatically.
Article 7: Persons who migrated from India to Pakistan after 1st March 1947 were not considered citizens of India, unless they returned to India with a permit for resettlement or permanent return.
Article 8: Persons of Indian origin residing outside India may acquire Indian citizenship by registering at the Indian embassy in their country of residence.
Article 9: Provided that if any person voluntarily acquired the citizenship of a foreign State, he/she will no longer be a citizen of India.
Article 10: Continuance of rights of citizenship.
Article 11: Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law.
Citizenship Act 1955:
Deals with the provisions of Citizenship after 26 Jan, 1950.
1. By Birth (sec-3)
Jus Soli (Right of Soil): Before 1 July 1987, any person born in India automatically acquired Indian citizenship, irrespective of the nationality of the parents.

Jus Sanguinis (Right of Blood): Due to concerns regarding illegal immigration, the law was amended. For persons born after 3 December 2003, citizenship by birth is granted only if at least one parent is an Indian citizen and the other is not an illegal immigrant at the time of birth.

2. By Descent (sec-4): A person born outside India can acquire Indian citizenship by descent if either of the parents is an Indian citizen and the birth is registered at the Indian consulate within one year of birth.
3. By registration (sec-5): granted to Indian-origin individuals, spouses of Indian citizens, or minor children who have resided in India for 7 years.
4. By Naturalisation (sec-6): granted to foreign nationals who have been —
Residing in India for 12 years (11 years in the preceding 14 years + 1 year immediately before application).
They must know one Indian Language mentioned in the 8th schedule.
Third Schedule of Citizenship Act 1955, mentions qualifications for Naturalisation.

Note: The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2003 provides that an illegal migrant cannot acquire Indian citizenship through registration or naturalization. It also laid the foundation for the creation of the National Register of Citizens (NRC).
5. By incorporating a territory (sec-7): When a new territory becomes part of India, the Government of India specifies which persons of that territory shall be granted Indian citizenship.
Can lose Citizenship through:
1. Renunciation (voluntarily gives up Indian citizenship)
2. Termination (voluntarily acquired citizenship of other country without informing)
3. Deprivation (if acquired citizenship by fraud, false documents, or during war helped an enemy country)
4, Disloyalty to the Constitution.
5. Continuous residence outside India for seven years.
6. Imprisonment for two years within five years after registration.
7. Communication or association with an enemy country during war.

Overseas Citizen of India (OCI)
The Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) Scheme was introduced in 2005 through an amendment to the Citizenship Act, 1955.
Note: The Person of Indian Origin (PIO) Scheme and the Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) Scheme were merged in 2015 to simplify the system for people of Indian origin living abroad.
Restrictions on OCI cardholders:
1) No right to vote in elections.
2) Not eligible for public services or government posts.
3) Not permitted to own agricultural property in India.
4) Indian passport is not issued to OCI holders, as they are foreign citizens.
Benefits for OCI cardholders:
1) Lifelong multiple-entry visa to visit India.
2) Facilities similar to NRIs in economic, financial, and educational fields.
3) Permission to buy or sell immovable property, except agricultural land, plantation property, or farmhouses.
4) Eligible to practice certain profession.
